items.stem: A firm competes by offering the fastest, most reliable delivery but manages operations purely to minimise cost. What is the strategic error?

options.text: Operations are not aligned with the firm's order-winning objectives
options.rationale: Correct: operations should support speed and dependability, its order-winners.

options.text: Cost should never be considered in operations
options.rationale: Cost matters, but not at the expense of the chosen order-winners.

options.text: Delivery speed is irrelevant to operations
options.rationale: Speed is a core operations performance objective here.

options.text: Operations have no link to strategy
options.rationale: Operations strategy is precisely about that link.

items.explanation: Correct: operations should support speed and dependability, its order-winners.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which statements about operations performance objectives are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Firms usually must make trade-offs between objectives
options.rationale: Correct: excelling everywhere at once is rarely feasible.

options.text: Order-winners are the objectives that most influence customer choice
options.rationale: Correct: order-winners directly win business in a given market.

options.text: A firm can be best-in-class at cost, quality, speed and flexibility simultaneously
options.rationale: Trade-offs usually prevent dominating every dimension at once.

options.text: Performance objectives are unrelated to competitive strategy
options.rationale: They are how operations delivers the competitive strategy.

items.explanation: Correct: excelling everywhere at once is rarely feasible.

items.stem: A plant adds capacity to every workstation to raise output but throughput barely improves. What was overlooked?

options.text: Output is limited by the bottleneck, so only relieving the constraint helps
options.rationale: Correct: adding capacity away from the constraint does not raise throughput.
Capacity matters, but specifically at the bottleneck.

options.text: Every workstation is always a bottleneck
options.rationale: Typically only the constraint limits throughput.

options.text: Throughput depends only on inventory levels
options.rationale: Throughput is governed by the constraint, not inventory alone.

items.explanation: Correct: adding capacity away from the constraint does not raise throughput.
